info.title: Evaluating hardware latencies with the hardware latency detector

abstract.para: The hardware latency detector (hwlatdetect) controls the kernel module (hwlat_detector.ko) and identifies system delays introduced directly by platform firmware and hardware independent of the operating system scheduler. This section describes how to configure your server BIOS settings for optimal low-latency performance. It guides you through executing the detector tool to isolate firmware bottlenecks before measuring kernel-level scheduling latencies.

topic.para: Before you run this test, verify that the platform firmware is optimized. Refer to for baseline optimization steps.

tip.para: Make sure the kernel-rt_debug package is installed on the system.

step.para: Log in as &rootuser; or run commands with sudo.
Start the detector with a specified threshold:
This command monitors system management interrupts with a minimum latency threshold of 10 microseconds.
Check the measured latencies. If the latencies do not meet your application deadlines, your hardware is not suitable. In this case, use a different hardware platform.
